subject: Culture
title: Caves and Underworlds
description: Learn Caves and Underworlds in one minute.

hook.text: Lascaux cave paintings are 17,000 years old. Some scholars believe the caves were cathedrals, not galleries.

buildup.text: Caves appear as sacred spaces in nearly every culture: Oracle at Delphi, Hindu cave temples, Maya cenotes.

discovery.text: Total darkness triggers sensory deprivation. Ancient cave rituals likely induced altered states of consciousness.

twist.text: Plato's 'Allegory of the Cave' used cave symbolism to teach philosophy. The cave represents ignorance.

climax.text: From womb to tomb, caves symbolize both origin and ending—the cycle cultures struggle to accept.

punchline.text: Humanity's first temples were holes in the ground.

quiz.question: How old are the Lascaux cave paintings?

details.summary: Caves have served as sacred spaces since the earliest human art — the Lascaux paintings date to 17,000 years ago. In many cultures, caves are portals to the underworld, places of origin myths, and sites where darkness enables spiritual transformation unavailable in daylight.
details.whyItMatters: Cave sacredness reveals humanity's oldest spiritual technology — using sensory deprivation (darkness, silence, confinement) to produce altered states of consciousness and encounters with the divine.
takeaways: Lascaux cave paintings date to approximately 17,000 years ago
Many cultures locate underworld entrances in caves
Cave darkness was used deliberately for spiritual transformation

faq.question: Why were caves used for spiritual rituals?
faq.answer: Total darkness eliminates visual input, heightening other senses and sometimes producing hallucinations. Cave acoustics create otherworldly echoes. The physical journey underground mirrors a psychological journey inward.

faq.question: Were cave paintings religious?
faq.answer: Most scholars believe cave art served spiritual or ritual purposes rather than pure decoration. Paintings are often placed in difficult-to-reach chambers, suggesting they were not for casual viewing. Many depict animals that were hunted, possibly for ritual power.
